reason: The hypothesis directly restates the well-established approach of cold rolling and annealing to refine and align lamellae in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloys, which multiple passages (P2, P7, P10, P15, P18, P20, P36, P39, P40) have already demonstrated or proposed as future work. The mechanism of reducing dislocation pile-ups by reorienting phase boundaries is also taken from the literature (P1, P13, P19, P21, P22, P26, P42). The predicted outcome of improved ductility with maintained strength mirrors results already reported in these passages. No new alloy, regime, mechanism, or integration of conflicting evidence is introduced; the hypothesis merely restates a known processing strategy and its known effects.
copied_elements: cold rolling + annealing to refine and align lamellae (P2, P7, P10, P15, P18, P20, P36, P39, P40)
reducing lamellar spacing and reorienting phase boundaries (P10, P15, P18, P25, P36)
minimizing dislocation pile-up and local stress concentration (P1, P13, P19, P21, P22, P26, P42)
improved ductility with maintained/increased strength (P2, P5, P7, P15, P18, P20, P23, P28, P36, P40)
baseline ~18% elongation with dislocation pile-ups at randomly oriented interfaces (P5, P19, P23)
falsification via EBSD and tensile testing (general knowledge)
